title: Grandfathered Equipment and Implicit MOC Acceptance
scenario_text:
Context from SAP S/4HANA (Equipment Master — Plant 3):
Equipment: FURN-301 (Batch Annealing Furnace #1) | Installed: 2009 | Last major overhaul: 2021 | Status: ACTIVE | Classification: PSM-covered process | Operating pressure: 45 psig | Max temp: 1,750°F | Linked PM orders: 47 active

**MasterControl — PSM Mechanical Integrity Records:**
FURN-301 last inspection: Jan 2026 | Result: SATISFACTORY | Inspector notes: 'Relief valve RV-301A tested at 52 psig (set point 50 psig). Within ±10% tolerance per API 576. Vessel wall thickness: 0.412" (minimum required: 0.375" per original design).'

**SharePoint — /engineering/standards/PSM-equipment-standards-2024.pdf (published Jul 2024)**
Section 6.2: 'All PSM-covered pressure vessels installed after January 1, 2015 must meet ASME Section VIII Div 1, 2017 Edition or later. Minimum wall thickness calculated per UG-27 with corrosion allowance of 0.0625".'
Section 6.4: 'Equipment installed prior to 2015 is exempt from Section 6.2 requirements PROVIDED it has undergone formal grandfathering review per MOC-EXT-001 process and maintains satisfactory mechanical integrity results.'

**Microsoft Teams — #engineering-standards (Mar 12, 2024, 2:15 PM)**
@janet.morrison (Process Engineering Director): Team — new PSM equipment standard is going out in July. We need to identify all pre-2015 equipment that needs grandfathering review. @miguel.santos can you pull the list for Plant 3?
@miguel.santos: Will do. Off the top of my head it's FURN-301, FURN-302, REAC-101, and the old quench tank QT-205.
@janet.morrison: Perfect. Let's get MOC-EXT-001 forms started for each. Target completion before the standard publishes.
@miguel.santos: 👍
[Thread has 2 additional replies — both from other plant managers confirming their lists]

**SAP — MOC (Management of Change) Log:**
MOC-2024-0045: FURN-302 grandfathering review | Status: APPROVED (Jun 2024)
MOC-2024-0046: REAC-101 grandfathering review | Status: APPROVED (Jun 2024)
MOC-2024-0047: QT-205 grandfathering review | Status: APPROVED (Jul 2024)
[No MOC record found for FURN-301]

**Email — Subject: 'Plant 3 Grandfathering Status' (Jun 28, 2024)**
From: miguel.santos@ironforge-mfg.com
To: janet.morrison@ironforge-mfg.com

'Janet — FURN-302, REAC-101, and QT-205 are all through MOC review and approved. FURN-301 is more complex — the original design calcs are missing from the files (pre-digital era). I'm working with the OEM to reconstruct them. Should have it wrapped up in a few weeks.'

**Janet Morrison's status in ADP: TERMINATED (Aug 15, 2024 — retirement)**
[No reply to Miguel's email found. No subsequent emails regarding FURN-301 grandfathering.]

**Maximo — Work Order History (FURN-301):**
47 completed PM work orders since Jul 2024 | 3 corrective maintenance orders | All signed off by qualified maintenance personnel | No operational restrictions noted | Equipment continuously operated for production since standard publication.
question: During a corporate PSM audit, the auditor asks: Is FURN-301 currently authorized to operate under Ironforge's PSM equipment standards? What is the correct finding?

contributor.name: Miguel Santos
contributor.title: Plant Operations Manager
contributor.domain_expertise: Production scheduling, maintenance planning, PSM compliance, equipment lifecycle management, Management of Change processes

choices: Authorized — Miguel's thumbs-up emoji in the Teams thread acknowledging the grandfathering task list, combined with 2 years of continued operation with management knowledge, constitutes implicit MOC approval
Not applicable — FURN-301 was installed in 2009 (pre-2015) and is therefore fully exempt from the 2024 standard under the pre-2015 installation clause in Section 6.2

Not authorized — FURN-301 lacks a completed MOC-EXT-001 grandfathering review as required by Section 6.4; the process was initiated but never completed due to the engineering director's departure, and no formal exemption or interim authorization exists in the system
Authorized — FURN-301 passes mechanical integrity inspections and has operated continuously since 2009; the satisfactory inspection results constitute de facto grandfathering acceptance
